maria_ops: Hey team — our Private control plane connectivity from our prod VPC started failing around 2026-03-15 21:40UTC. App logs show TLS/mTLS handshake failures to controlplane.redwood.example.com and retries time out. We rolled nothing on our side.
alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, we'll triage. Can you paste the exact error from your client logs? Also which control plane FQDN/IP are you hitting?
maria_ops: Logs show: `tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad certificate` and the app stacktrace ends with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` even though we've uploaded the client cert to Redwood and your onboarding check passed last month. We're talking to `controlplane-eu.private.redwood.internal:443` (resolves to 10.2.33.12 via our DNS).
alex_support: Hm. Two quick checks: 1) can you run `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.33.12:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -servername controlplane-eu.private.redwood.internal -msg` from a host in the same subnet and paste output? 2) can you tcpdump the 3-way TLS exchange: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/mtls.pcap -s 0 host 10.2.33.12 and port 443` and attach? ci-bot: created ticket INF-4921.
maria_ops: ran openssl. Result truncated but here's the key part: ``
CONNECTED(00000003)
>>> TLS 1.3 Handshake [length 0040]
>>> ClientHello
<<< TLS 1.3 Alert [length 0002]
<<< fatal handshake_failure
140123456789120:error:141740A7:SSL routines:ssl23_read_bytes:ssl handshake failure:../ssl/ssl_lib.c:1411
``
And tcpdump shows a SYN, then TLS ClientHello from our IP, then RST from the egress appliance, not from Redwood IP. Attaching pcap shortly.
jordan_netops: If appliance is sending RST after ClientHello that suggests an inline proxy/NAT is unhappy with TLS metadata. Does your egress path include a TLS-intercepting NGFW or a cloud egress gateway that might inspect/terminate mTLS? Many of those will drop or rewrap client certs.
maria_ops: Yes we have a third-party egress appliance (Corp-NAT) that transparently inspects TLS to block data exfil. We thought it was passthrough for internal hosts though.
alex_support: Two likely failure modes: 1) the appliance is performing TLS termination and not forwarding the client certificate to the upstream (so Redwood control plane never sees client cert). 2) it's rewriting the ClientHello (SNI or extensions) or changing ALPN/cipher list and triggering handshake failure. Can you test bypassing the appliance (egress rule allowing direct to 10.2.33.12) from a single host?
maria_ops: Tried bypass by spinning a temporary instance in a subnet with NAT bypass. From there openssl completes fine and control plane accepts the client cert. So bypass works.
sam_oncall: That confirms the egress appliance is the culprit. Two remediation options: add controlplane FQDN/IPs to the egress bypass/allowlist or configure the NGFW to not terminate/inspect TLS for our mTLS destinations. For the former, note our control plane uses multiple IPs and rotates during rolling deployments — best to allow by SNI (`controlplane-eu.private.redwood.internal`) in the egress rule, or add the Redwood regional IP CIDR we provided in onboarding.
lee_security: Quick note: if you add by SNI, make sure the appliance does not rewrite SNI. Also verify the appliance supports passthrough of client certs for mutual TLS (some proxies can do TLS rewrap but still forward cert info via headers — Redwood requires real mTLS so that won't work). We need full end-to-end mTLS.
maria_ops: The NGFW does TLS inspection by default and we saw earlier a rule to "inspect internal TLS". Looks like that rule rewraps TLS. How can we confirm it's rewrapping vs just dropping the client cert? Any packet-level signatures we should look for?
alex_support: In a rewrap/terminate+re-init flow you'll see two separate TLS sessions on the wire: 1) client->proxy ClientHello, 2) proxy->upstream new ClientHello. The proxy will present a different server cert to the client. In a pure passthrough you'll only see one ClientHello and a continuous handshake to the upstream IP. You already saw a RST from the appliance which implies it actively terminated. If you can share the pcap we can check the cert chain presented to the client.
maria_ops: Uploaded `/tmp/mtls.pcap` to the ticket. CI-bot: INF-4921 updated with attachment.
alex_support: Thanks. I opened the pcap — proxy is presenting a proxy-signed server cert to the client (Issuer: Corp-Inspect CA). It then opens a separate connection to Redwood control plane without presenting the original client cert. So Redwood never gets the client cert -> handshake fails. Root cause: transparent TLS inspection is terminating mTLS.
jordan_netops: For a fix: 1) add exact controlplane hostnames to the NGFW TLS-bypass list so it doesn't intercept those FQDNs; OR 2) if bypass by hostname isn't possible, add the regional IP ranges Redwood provided to a passthrough ACL. Prefer option 1 to avoid future IP churn. Also ensure the bypass applies to mTLS ports (443) and doesn't accidentally apply only to HTTP.
maria_ops: We'll request the NGFW team add the FQDN to the bypass list. In the meantime, is there a temporary workaround like rotating to a different control plane endpoint we can route to?
alex_support: We can provision a temporary fixed-IP endpoint for your org (short-lived) if you need an immediate workaround while NGFW rules are updated. I'll escalate in the ticket and provide an IP and cert chain to pin. Also attaching recommended test commands:

```
# test direct mTLS handshake
openssl s_client -connect controlplane-eu.private.redwood.internal:443 \
  -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile redwood_root_ca.pem -servername controlplane-eu.private.redwood.internal -tls1_2 -msg

# tcpdump capture filter
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w mtls.pcap host <controlplane_ip> and port 443
```
sam_oncall: Also please watch for the NGFW's OCSP/CRL fetch behaviour — some appliances block outbound OCSP which can cause cert validation to fail mid-handshake. If adding bypass doesn't work, we may need to validate OCSP reachability to our OCSP responders.
lee_security: After they add bypass, we recommend a short audit: 1) confirm client->upstream TLS shows single ClientHello and server cert chain is Redwood's, 2) run `curl --cert client.pem --key client.key --cacert redwood_root_ca.pem https://controlplane-eu.private.redwood.internal/health` from a host behind the same path.
maria_ops: NGFW team added `controlplane-eu.private.redwood.internal` to TLS bypass. After propagation (5 min) our app connections resumed and all mTLS handshakes succeed. Thanks for the quick help.
alex_support: Great to hear — marking INF-4921 as resolved pending your verification in 24h. If you want, we can also add the explicit regional IP CIDR to your onboarding docs so the bypass is durable.
maria_ops: Please do. Also, can you document the config guidance for NGFW vendors (Palo Alto, Fortinet) in the ticket? The NGFW team wants vendor-specific steps.
alex_support: Will attach vendor-specific notes to the ticket (Palo Alto: SSL Forward Proxy exception for SNI host; FortiGate: add to SSL/SSH inspection exclusion list by FQDN). Closing here but keeping INF-4921 open for the docs attachment. :thumbsup:
